semin-durr:2-2.t: His saying: {وَطُورِ سِينِينَ}: الطُّور is a mountain, and سينين is the name of a place, so the mountain was annexed to the place where it is. Al-Zamakhsharī said: «It is like سِينون and يَبْرُوْن in the permissibility of inflecting with wāw and yāʾ, of keeping the yāʾ fixed and moving the nūn with the inflectional vowels.» Abū al-Baqāʾ said: «It is a dialectal form of سَيْناء.» End of quotation. The majority read it with kasra on the sīn, and Ibn Abī Isḥāq, ʿAmr ibn Maymūn and Abū Rajāʾ with fatḥa on it, which is the dialect of Bakr and Tamīm. ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, ʿAbd Allāh [ibn Masʿūd], al-Ḥasan and Ṭalḥa read «سِيْناءَ» with kasra and the prolongation (madd); and ʿUmar also, and Zayd ibn ʿAlī, with fatḥa and the prolongation. Both have been mentioned in [Sūrat] al-Muʾminūn. These are dialectal forms that differ in this Syriac name, in keeping with the Arabs' custom of playing with foreign names. Al-Akhfash said: «سينين is trees, the singular سِيْنِية.» This is very strange and not known from the exegetes.

semin-durr:3-3.t: His saying: {الأمين}: This is فَعيل for intensification, i.e. those in it and those who enter it are safe — humans, birds and animals. It may also be from أَمُنَ الرجلُ with ḍamma on the mīm, أمانةً, so he is أمين (trustworthy); and its trustworthiness is its guarding those who enter it, just as the trustworthy person guards what he is entrusted with. It may also be in the sense of a passive participle (mafʿūl), from أَمِنَه (he felt safe from it), because it is safe from calamities.

semin-durr:4-4.t:
His saying: {لَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا}: This is what is sworn upon.
His saying: {في أَحْسَنِ تَقْوِيم}: an adjective of an omitted [noun], i.e. "in a fashioning that is the best fashioning". Abū al-Baqāʾ said: «"في أحسنِ تقويم" is in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) of "الإِنسان"; by التقويم he meant القَوام (upright form), because التقويم is an act, and that is an attribute of the Creator, not of the created. It is also possible that the implied form is: "in the best form of fashioning", the muḍāf having been omitted. It is also possible that "في" is redundant (zāʾida), i.e. "قَوَّمْناه أحسنَ تقويم" (We fashioned him with the best fashioning).» End of quotation. There is no need for these strained interpretations.

semin-durr:5-5.t: His saying: {أَسْفَلَ سَافِلِينَ}: Two views are possible on it. The first: it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the object. The second: it is an adjective of an omitted place, i.e. "to a place lowest of the low". ʿAbd Allāh [ibn Masʿūd] read «السَّافِلين» with the definite article.

semin-durr:6-6.t: His saying: {إِلاَّ الذين آمَنُواْ}: There are two views on it. The first: it is a conjoined exception (muttaṣil), on the meaning: We returned him lower than [all] the low in creation and composition, i.e. uglier than His [other] creation and most deformed in form, and they are the people of the Fire; so the connection on this view is clear. The second: it is a disjoined exception (munqaṭiʿ), on the meaning: then after that fashioning and beautifying, We returned him lower than [all] the low in the best of form and shape, in that We reversed him in his constitution, so that his back became bent and his sight and hearing weakened; and the meaning is: but those of the decrepit who were righteous will have a lasting reward. Al-Zamakhsharī said this, [here] summarised.

semin-durr:7-7.t: His saying: {فَمَا يُكَذِّبُكَ}: «ما» is interrogative, in the position of a nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), and the khabar (predicate) is the verb after it. The one addressed is man, by way of a shift of address (iltifāt); it was also said: the one addressed is the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. On the first [view] the meaning is: what makes you a liar because of the Judgement (الدِّين) and its denial after this proof? I.e. you lie when you deny the recompense, because everyone who denies the truth is a liar; so what thing compels you to be a liar because of the recompense? The bāʾ is like the one in His saying, the Exalted: {على الذين يَتَوَلَّوْنَهُ والذين هُم بِهِ مُشْرِكُونَ} [al-Naḥl: 100]. On the second [view] the meaning is: what then is it that gives you the lie in what you report of the recompense and the resurrection — which is الدِّين — after these lessons, reflection on which necessitates the truth of what you have said? Al-Farrāʾ and al-Akhfash said this.
